proposals.rationale: Identifies the explicit exception relaxing the baseline requirement in C0011 that a court order or decree must list both current and former names, applying when an adjudicator receives a court order making the former name confidential.
proposals.quote: EXCEPTION: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program).

fields.logic_text: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program)

fields.summary: Relaxes the baseline requirement that a court order or decree must list both current and former names when an adjudicator receives a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (such as under California's Safe at Home program).

proposals.rationale: Identifies the qualification embedded in NOTE under 8 FAM 403.1-3(B) governing C0018, establishing an explicit exception to the family name spacing consistency recommendation when an individual family member clearly expresses a preference for different spacing.
proposals.quote: unless a family member expresses a clear preference for a different spacing.

fields.summary: An adjudicator is not required to space family members' last names consistently if an individual family member clearly expresses a preference for different spacing.

observations.quote: Name spacing issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
observations.rationale: The rule establishing that name spacing issues generally do not justify rewriting a passport is already fully captured by claim C0028.

observations.quote: Some applicants may include the prefix “Sr.” as an abbreviation for “Señor” in Spanish meaning “Mr.” or “Mister” in English.
observations.rationale: The statement regarding the prefix 'Sr.' being used for 'Señor' is already represented by claim C0029.

observations.quote: If you determine that this is the case, follow the guidance in 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) regarding ranks and titles.
observations.rationale: The requirement to follow 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) when 'Sr.' is determined to mean 'Señor' is already captured by claim C0030.

observations.quote: Name suffix issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
observations.rationale: The rule that name suffix issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport is already represented by claim C0031.
